title: ChatGPT for stock info
author: JoRyder7
selftext: Is anyone using CHATGPT to help with weekly stock buys? If so, how has it been working out? I am completely new to this and am looking for some advice. I have been putting in about $100 a week and am currently up for the year about 11%.

comments.author: Golden_Age_Fallacy
comments.body: VOO is up 13% YTD, might just want to stick with that and avoid extra token costs.

replies.author: JoRyder7
replies.body: A portion in my portfolio is in VOO. I also have a couple blue chips. But am taking some risks with a few moonshots.

replies.author: teckel
replies.body: Planned moonshots more commonly end up bag-holders. Better to just invest in index funds. Using GPT to pick stocks without starting with deterministic research, proper llm prompting, followed by more deterministic gates will probably underperform market indexes.

replies.author: JoRyder7
replies.body: My moonshots only make up about 5% of my entire portfolio. What I’ve put in I can afford to. Been told to treat it like a lottery ticket.

comments.author: Enough-Beginning3687
comments.body: I don't use chatgpt but I use an AI for options trading picks called BrokerBotics. The problem is that whole chatgpt etc are great for analyzing specific stocks, they aren't great for scanning the market to pick stocks. I think if you already have a stock in mind, it's great but picking stocks, not that much.

replies.author: JoRyder7
replies.body: I would agree with that. Been trying to build an AI/tech portfolio. Chat didn’t catch the Dell stock uptick. How do you like BrokerBotics?

replies.author: Enough-Beginning3687
replies.body: I use it for a specific purpose - to help me run a 1% a week strategy with cash secured put options. It's been great so far. I've been running the strategy for 24 weeks. So far it's the only AI I've found that can scan the full market real time. It's not perfect because it will hallucinate with complex questions and it sometimes doesn't have all the data, like you can't ask it about intra-day stuff. Overall my goal is to reduce my trading time to 15 mins a week and it's been great for that. Also I can just dm the founder on discord and they'll fix any issues. Like when I started it would take 4 minutes for my weekly option scan. Now it takes 30 seconds.

replies.author: JoRyder7
replies.body: Thank you. I will check it out.

comments.author: Strict-Amphibian-830
comments.body: I use an LLM for a Warren Buffet type analysis on companies for long term considerations.  I also will ask about stocks to watch for the day or week for quick ins and outs.  An LLM with more real time data would probably be best, but I don’t have access to one

comments.author: Kozue_Sawada
comments.body:
I use ChatGPT and a few other AI tools too, mainly to analyze info, challenge my ideas and turn the data into charts / visual reports. But I wouldn’t let AI decide what I buy.
I get the numbers from verified data, Python or a spreadsheet. Then I use AI to look for risks, explain unusual periods and give me both the bull + bear case. I still check the important stuff against filings and make the final call myself.
For backtests, point-in-time data and OOS testing are a must... otherwise AI can easily introduce look-ahead bias.
11% is a nice result btw, but I’d also check it vs a benchmark, max drawdown and portfolio concentration.
Basically: AI helps me research and visualize, reliable data does the math, and I make the decision.
